summary: Deduplicate the blind re-audit findings that match no ledger item, verify each distinct error against the full repository, and check which paper claims they affect

clusters.title: SAE annotation: BH run only on tests that already had raw p<0.1
clusters.description: Hypergeometric enrichment rows are kept only when overlap>=2 and raw p<0.1. Benjamini-Hochberg is then applied to those kept rows only (about 27k-34k rows), not to all feature x term tests (about 6-12 million per layer). The spec (01-sae-atlas.md:182) asks for BH over all terms for each feature. Every kept 'significant' row has raw p<=0.042, so the step is nearly uncorrected. Recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv: per-feature BH over 2,369 terms leaves 4.2% (L0), 1.7% (L5), 1.1% (L11) of features annotated; global BH leaves 29, 5 and 0 features. Reported: 80.7/67.8/61.7%. 79-85% of hits rest on an overlap of 2 genes in a top-20 list. The annotation rates, the 12-layer U-shape, 'more interpretable than Geneformer (52.4%)' and every downstream use of the labels (Phase 6 'richly annotated' picks, Stage-2 source selection, circuit coherence, Phase 10, Stage-3 annotated/unannotated split) are affected. Not in the ledger.

clusters.title: SAE modules: '10 modules' is a hard-coded fallback setting
clusters.location: runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phases2_to_8.py:370-381 (n_clusters=min(10,n_alive) at 373, pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] at 376, labels to alive_idx at 379); runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/full_12layer_pipeline.py:299-312; runs/sae-atlas-217M/outputs/phases2_to_8.log:78; summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:48-58,84
clusters.description: leidenalg was not installed (log line 78). Both scripts silently fell back to SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10, n_alive)). So every layer has exactly 10 modules and every alive feature gets a label (coverage = alive fraction) by construction. The summary scores '10 modules at 99.9-100% coverage, matches the paper's 6-12 precisely' as a replication, and the 12-layer summary repeats '120 modules'. The spec requires Leiden. Second, smaller bug: the 3-layer fallback clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] (the first n_alive indices, not the alive features) and writes labels to alive_idx, which mislabels L0 (2,430 dead). Two verifiers found the saved module_labels.npy came from the 12-layer run, which indexes correctly with np.ix_, so the saved labels and coverage are not hit by the indexing bug; one verifier says Phase 10 used the 3-layer labels.

clusters.title: SAE persistence: 3-layer and 12-layer summaries reach opposite verdicts
clusters.description: The 3-layer summary marks 'features overwhelmingly layer-specific, no persistent scaffold' as a replication (tick). It compares non-adjacent L0->L5 (2.5%) with the paper's adjacent L0->L1. The 12-layer summary of the same SAEs reports L6->L7 21.5% and L0->L8 13.3% and says 'dramatically higher persistence than Geneformer, differs from paper'. The tick was never revised. Persistence is decoder cosine >0.7 between separately trained SAEs, with no seed-to-seed baseline, so neither verdict has a null. The annotation-by-depth profile is also called 'declining' in one summary and 'U-shaped' in the other (and both rest on N01).

clusters.title: 12-layer summary misreports adjacent persistence values
clusters.description: The 12-layer summary gives L0->L1 0.5%, L1->L2 3.3% and L2->L3 1.6%. The logs show 0/4928 (0.0%), 8/4928 (0.2%) and 45/4928 (0.9%). The summary numbers match no file.

clusters.title: Dead SAE features counted as alive (no-op alive check)
clusters.location: runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phases2_to_8.py:242 (alive = array.shape[0] > 0, always True, unused), :292 (n_src_alive = decoder norm > 1e-8); runs/sae-atlas-217M/outputs/phase3/svd_comparison.csv; outputs/phase4/cross_layer_tracking.csv
clusters.description: The 'alive' flag at line 242 is always True and never used. Persistence uses n_src_alive = count of decoder columns with norm > 1e-8, but decoders are unit-normalised every step, so all 4,928 columns count. At L0, 2,430 dead features are counted as 'novel' (4,928/4,928) and enter the persistence denominator. The novelty percentage barely changes (no L0 feature is aligned either way). The persistence rate does: L0->L5 is 125/2,498 = 5.0% of alive features, not the 2.5% said to 'match the paper'. All 12-layer L0->Lx rates are halved the same way. Alive counts also differ between tables (L5 4,903 vs 4,928; L11 4,813 vs 4,924), which verifiers judged trivial (eval split vs all positions).

clusters.title: 'Massive superposition confirmed' uses a test any dictionary passes
clusters.description: A feature counts as 'SVD-aligned' only if its decoder has |cos| > 0.7 with one of the top 50 singular vectors in 1,232-d. A random unit vector has max |cos| of about 0.07-0.13 with 50 orthonormal directions (simulated: 0 of 4,928 random vectors exceed 0.7). So about 100% 'novel' is expected for any dictionary, including a random one. No random-dictionary or shuffled control was run. The metric copies the source paper, so the number is a faithful replication; the error is the claim 'massive superposition confirmed'.

clusters.title: 12-layer pipeline writes SVD-alignment results without running the test
clusters.description: The 12-layer pipeline sets n_svd_aligned=0 and n_novel=n_alive with a comment 'computed below' that is never computed, and writes svd_comparison.json with total_svd_aligned 0 and pct_novel 1.0. These hard-coded values feed the 12-layer summary and atlas. Checked in code. The real values are close (99.9-100%), so the numeric impact is small, but the 12-layer superposition result is not measured.

clusters.title: 'Information highways 99.6-100%' has no null and no minimum co-occurrence
clusters.description: A source feature is a 'highway' if its maximum PMI over about 4,928 target features exceeds 3. PMI is computed even for a single co-occurrence, and there is no minimum count and no null. For rare features one co-occurrence already gives PMI > 3, and same-position continuity across layers inflates PMI. So 99.6-100% is close to guaranteed. 'Replicates exactly' and 'dense computational cascades across depth' are unsupported. The metric comes from the spec, so the replication number is like-for-like; the reading is not.

clusters.title: Phase 10 'unannotated features co-activate with annotated' is ~100% by construction
clusters.description: An unannotated feature counts as co-activating if it shares any of the 10 forced spectral modules (about 490 features each, see N02) with any annotated feature. With about 65% of features 'annotated' (inflated, see N01), every module holds an annotated feature, so 99.8-100% follows by construction. The scorecard 'replicates' row has no null.

clusters.title: Phase 11 cell-type enrichment tests token positions as independent
clusters.description: '95.9% of features cell-type enriched' comes from Fisher tests over about 1.75M token positions from 1,000 cells. Positions in one cell share its type, so this is pseudoreplication. Correction is Bonferroni over 32 cell types only, not over features; the spec asks for BH. Partly overlaps L123, which records that Phase 11 also applies the L5 SAE to the wrong layer; the unit-of-analysis problem here is separate.

clusters.title: Phase 8 'perturbation response' proxy is a token-identity test scored as a replication
clusters.description: For each target gene G the proxy compares SAE activations at positions where token G itself appears against random other positions. That detects token identity, not a perturbation, and it runs 4,928 uncorrected Mann-Whitney tests per target. Detection is 60/60 (1.0). Both scorecards (lines 85 and 141) still mark 'perturbation detection 92% vs 100%' as replicated, even after the true-CRISPRi run gave 0.04. Partly overlaps L020/L021 (the 0/48 true-perturbation test, and L021's note on the multi-tissue table comparing proxy detection rates), but the invalid proxy and its scorecard tick are not in the ledger.

clusters.title: Phase 6 patching drops the SAE reconstruction error; no reconstruction-only baseline
clusters.description: Phase 6 replaces the whole hidden state with sae.decode(z with feature f zeroed). It never adds back the reconstruction error (about 11% unexplained variance) and has no reconstruction-only baseline. The logit change is then dominated by a feature-independent effect: mean off-target delta is 1.394-1.396 for every feature and target delta 1.39-1.44, so ratios sit near 1 (median 1.015). 'Target' means positions whose input token is one of the feature's top-20 genes, not those genes' output logits. The '1.01x genuine non-replication' is a method artefact. Separate from the wrong-layer bug (L031) and from the paper's description of the ratio (L032).

clusters.title: Cross-reference claims unannotated features carry 'disproportionate' causal influence
clusters.description: The cross-reference says unannotated features 'carry a disproportionate share of downstream causal influence' and that annotation-led tracing 'systematically missed the most important hubs'. The data show top-20 hubs 55% annotated against a 50% pool fixed by design (500+500), Fisher not significant; top-100 also n.s. So unannotated features are at or below parity. The same section cites a '~50% unannotated pool' while the atlas reports 67.8% annotated at L5, and says Phase 6 tested '30' features when it used 50. It uses this to dismiss the Phase 6 null. Partly overlaps L011, which notes the hub counts are block-deletion artefacts; the misreading of 55% vs 50% is a separate error.

clusters.title: '~5K edges per feature in both experiments' is false
clusters.description: The exhaustive summary says per-feature density is consistent at about 5K edges per feature in Stage 2 and Exp 1. Stage 2 has 2,144,011/120 = 17,867 edges per feature; Exp 1 has 4,970. Partly overlaps L011 (Exp-1 edge counts are block-deletion artefacts) and L017 (other exhaustive summary numbers that do not match files), but this number is not listed there.

clusters.title: L0 (static token embedding) read as a computing layer; '12 layers' for 11 blocks
clusters.description: L0 is hidden_states[0], the embedding output: a function of token ID only, with about 6.3k distinct vectors. L0 SAE features are just partitions of gene identity, and the 49% dead rate follows from that. Claims such as 'L0 features are essential for the entire computation', 'early-layer broadcast hubs replicate' and 'L0 steering pushes toward maturity' describe embedding properties (or the block-deletion artefact). The circuit-tracing scope says '12 layers' though config has 11 blocks, and Geneformer's L0-L17 are block outputs, so L0 comparisons are not like-for-like. The SAE summaries do label L0 '(post-embed)', so this is mainly interpretive. Same root cause as L047 (spectral CKA at L0), different pipeline and claims.

clusters.title: Architecture and field-wide claims drawn from one model under one condition
clusters.description: Only MaxToki (217M, plus one 1B attention run) was run in these harnesses, with 500 K562 cells, one SAE seed and 200 K562 cells for tracing. Yet the summaries say: 'single-cell foundation models, regardless of architecture, have not internalised causal regulatory wiring'; 'the limitation is in MaxToki's representations'; the depth hierarchy 'is specific to bidirectional BERT-style encoders'; the VW asymmetry is 'likely specific to causal Llama decoders' (the 1B model already peaks at L4-L5, not L1); 'consequence of decoder-only training on trajectories'. No encoder or other model was run for comparison. Partly overlaps L085 (cross-pipeline 'five probes converge') and L021 (its note on 'the limitation is in MaxToki's representations').

clusters.title: Circuit 'biological coherence 36.1%' has no chance baseline
clusters.description: Coherence is the share of edges whose source and target features share any annotation term (36.1% vs the paper's 52.9%). No random-pair or permuted-pairing baseline exists in circuit_trace.py or remaining_phases.py. A quick check gives about 10-13% for random annotated pairs, but sources were picked for rich annotation, so the right chance level is unknown. The annotations themselves come from the uncorrected Phase 2 (N01). 'Lower coherence means broader, less specific features' is unanchored. Partly overlaps L005 (its notes list 36.1% coherence among numbers built on block-deleting edges) and L006 (same missing-null pattern for edge density).

clusters.title: Exp 3 'pseudotime' is PC1 of mixed immune cells; 'temporal information everywhere' unsupported
clusters.description: 'Pseudotime' is PC1 of log1p expression over 200 random Tabula Sapiens immune cells of mixed types, rescaled to [0,1]; early/late are its quartiles. That axis mostly tracks cell type, not maturation, and is never validated. The SAEs were trained on K562. The switch criterion was relaxed from the spec's Cohen's d>0.9 to |rho|>0.3. The headline '5,767 switch features ... temporal information permeates every layer' (vs the paper's 14) and steering read as 'toward maturity' are unsupported. Two sub-points from the audits are wrong: multiple testing does not matter (|rho|>0.3 at n=200 gives p about 1.6e-5), and the summary's cos(g_early,g_late) = 0.999 is itself a misreport (file gives 0.881), which is ledger L017. The proxy is disclosed as a deviation. Partly overlaps L015 (steering results are block-deletion artefacts) and L017.

clusters.title: Wrong gene biology used to support steering (FTL 'terminal erythroid', SOD3/KITLG 'stemness')
clusters.description: FTL (ferritin light chain) is called a 'terminal erythroid/mature marker' and used as evidence that steering is 'biologically coherent ... push toward maturity'. FTL is a ubiquitous iron-storage gene, highest in macrophages, and the cells are Tabula Sapiens immune. The top upregulated list is FTL plus mitochondrial and housekeeping genes (MT-CO3, MT-ND1, FTH1, PABPC1, UBC). SOD3 (extracellular superoxide dismutase) and KITLG are called progenitor/stemness factors with no support. Partly overlaps L015, which shows the steering results themselves are artefacts; the wrong labels are a separate error.

clusters.title: Attention edge read from one direction of a causal mask, so it partly measures expression rank
clusters.location: runs/attention-grn-217M/scripts/phase0_extract.py:281-301 (sum over all ordered pairs, divide by pair_counts); runs/attention-grn-217M/scripts/phase1_trivial_baselines.py:265-275 (row = attn[pert_hvg,:]); runs/attention-grn-217M/README.md:85
clusters.description: MaxToki is a causal decoder over genes ordered by expression rank. attn[query=P, key=T] is structurally zero whenever T ranks below P in a cell. phase0 averages over every cell with both genes, zeros included, so each edge is roughly P(T ranked above P) x attention, a gene-level rank property. Phases 1/3 use only the query=source row. No transpose, symmetrised or rank-conditioned edge is ever tested. The README discloses the directed form but says the pipeline 'handles it'. This weakens 'attention captures co-expression, not regulation' and 'replicates in a causal decoder'. Verifiers judged it unlikely to flip verdicts where gene variance beats attention by 0.06-0.20 AUROC; the edge tensors are not saved, so size cannot be checked.

clusters.title: Phase 4 head ablation cannot test 'heads are not a causal bottleneck'
clusters.description: Top-5 'TRRUST heads' at L1/L2/L4 are masked at their o_proj input, and the readout is the TRRUST AUROC of layer-mean L8 attention, whose baseline is 0.440 (below chance), on 300 cells and 8 TFs. Nothing measures model output or perturbation prediction (the spec's Phase 4 endpoint, with fidelity checks, 13 conditions and 2,000 cells). There is one draw per condition, no CI and no positive control; random-5 deltas span -0.015 to +0.018 and head (0,6) is in all three random sets; best-layer AUROC rose (0.684 to 0.697) under top-5 masking. Head ranking used the same 8 TFs (winner's curse), and the L1 TRRUST AUROC 0.684 is never reported or null-tested. 'Not a causal bottleneck' and 'the same causal null the paper reports' are unsupported. One audit sub-claim is false: the 300 cells are a subset of the Phase 0 cells. Overall FAIL still rests on C1/C2.

clusters.title: Phase 0b value-weighted vs attention AUROCs misquoted
clusters.description: The summary says 'VW per-pert AUROC = 0.513 vs raw attention 0.532' at L8. The files give 0.4933 vs 0.5119. The difference (-0.019) and p (0.012) are right, and the summary's own CSSI table uses 0.5119, so the conclusion stands; the quoted values are wrong.

clusters.title: 'Architectural asymmetry' compares different endpoints; VW TRRUST never null-tested
clusters.description: The summary contrasts raw attention peaking at L1 (0.553, per-perturbation AUROC) with VW peaking at L9-L10 (about 0.59, TRRUST AUROC) and calls it an 'architectural asymmetry'. These are different metrics. Like for like, VW per-pert is below 0.5 at L0-L8 (0.458-0.493) and peaks at 0.515 (L9). The summary also says this 'rules out both attention-pattern and value-pathway explanations', but the VW TRRUST values (0.588/0.587, the highest attention-derived TRRUST in the run) were never tested against the curveball or label nulls, and raw-attention TRRUST rests on 66 edges with null SD 0.043.

clusters.title: CSSI test run on degenerate clusters (four single-cell clusters)
clusters.description: KMeans K=10 gave cluster sizes [814,1,261,1,1,1,3,14,310,594]. CSSI-max and CSSI-mean are unweighted over clusters, so one-cell clusters get full weight; the 'oracle cluster max' 0.5017 is a size-1 cluster. 'Two of three aggregations significantly worse' and 'CSSI fails to rescue attention' reflect a broken stratification, not a test of the method. The summary does note the skew and limits the claim to homogeneous NT controls.

clusters.title: TRRUST endpoint rests on 8-32 TFs with edges pooled as independent
clusters.description: TRRUST conclusions (C3, C4, curveball, CSSI) use 8 TFs/66 edges (K562), 16/173 (RPE1), 32/281 (Adamson) and 12/96 (1B). Edges sharing a TF are pooled into one AUROC. The K562 label-shuffle null SD is 0.043, so differences of 0.01-0.04 are noise. Overall FAIL verdicts rest on the per-perturbation tests, so impact is on the TRRUST-based statements. Partly overlaps L036, whose notes say the TRRUST test is small; L036's error is the missing gene-level baseline.

clusters.title: C3 retention ratio is undefined when the baseline is below 0.5
clusters.description: C3 is (auc - 0.5) / max(baseline - 0.5, 1e-6). For K562 the TRRUST baseline is 0.483, so C3 = -13,421 (GBDT -2,957) and FAIL is forced by the formula, not the data. Adamson 'passes' with 1.03 on a 0.5195 baseline. Partly overlaps L037 (its note that K562 raw TRRUST is already below chance, so nothing can 'collapse') and L035 (C3 threshold looser than spec), but the broken formula itself is not in the ledger.

clusters.title: Attention-GRN negative has no positive control or planted-signal check
clusters.location: runs/attention-grn-217M/scripts/ (no synthetic or detectability phase; spec Phases 8 and 10 skipped per verdict scope_notes); summaries/attention-grn-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:3-16
clusters.description: 'FAIL on all four runs' is a null result, but the pipeline never shows it can find planted regulatory signal: no synthetic planted-edge test and no real positive control (e.g. ChIP-backed K562 targets). The verifier notes the harness does detect gene-level signal (gene-variance AUROC 0.596-0.766), and the main verdict is comparative, so the gap mainly weakens the 8-TF TRRUST arguments. The ledger records the same gap for circuit tracing (L010), exhaustive mapping (L019), H123 (L061) and longevity (L083), not for attention-GRN.

clusters.title: CRISPRi 54.6% cited as an attention-GRN Phase 11 result
clusters.description: The attention-GRN summary credits 'Phase-11 CRISPRi 54.6%' to this pipeline. Its verdict scope_notes list Phase 11 as skipped; the number comes from circuit tracing. L001 already notes the (invalid) 54.6% value was quoted in this summary; the wrong attribution is the new part.

clusters.title: Cross-dataset report flips the sign of the top-5 head-ablation delta
clusters.description: The report gives the top-5 head ablation change as +0.0051; ablation_results.csv gives delta_primary -0.00514. No verdict changes.

clusters.title: Attention-GRN README still lists Phase 0b and 5-11 as skipped
clusters.description: The README lists Phase 0b and Phases 5-11 as skipped, while the final summary reports 0b and CSSI (Phase 6) results. Stale documentation only.

clusters.title: Lineage TwoNN dimension estimated from 6-9 points with no size-matched null
clusters.description: Lineage TwoNN uses 6 B-cell and 9 T-cell marker genes in 1,232-d (Myeloid has 1, NaN). After the F<0.9 mask the fit uses about 5 points (phases_67's own _twonn allows 3; the Phase 1 version needs 10). Estimates are noise: ID 101 from 6 points, then 34, 34, 62, 34. Global TwoNN falls 102 to 6.7, and no random gene set of the same size was tested, so any subset would 'compress'. 'B-cell compression replicated (rho -0.867)', 'T-cell divergent' and 'geometry encodes time rather than lineage identity' are unsupported. The source paper also used tiny marker sets, so the weakness is partly inherited.

clusters.title: Audit row 16 calls BATF-to-PAX5 divergence 'distance metrics replicate strongly'
clusters.location: summaries/spectral-geometry-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md (spec audit row 16; vs Key finding #10 and lines 97-103); runs/spectral-geometry-217M/outputs/phase7/depth_correlations.json
clusters.description: depth_correlations.json gives dist_BATF_to_PAX5 vs depth rho = +0.979 (distance grows, i.e. divergence; the paper reports about -0.97). Row 16 nonetheless says 'distance metrics replicate strongly', which contradicts the summary's own Key finding #10. rank_BATF rho is 0.371 (p 0.23), not convergence.

clusters.title: Phase 9b 'paper's null does not replicate' compares a different statistic and null
clusters.description: MaxToki vs Geneformer static-embedding alignment (Pearson of off-diagonal similarities 0.382) is called 'IS significant (p=0)' and the paper's p>0.3 is called a non-replication. The null here is a gene-label shuffle (mean 0, SD 0.001), which any shared structure beats. The paper's result was a raw cosine under a shared-vocabulary null. The two models share the identical tokenizer and the gene-median file, so a label shuffle cannot support 'not an artefact of vocabulary order'. The verifier notes the spec does ask for a permutation test, and the alignment value is computed correctly; the error is the non-replication claim. Partly overlaps L116 (paper overstates the cross-model section, including the 0.382 bar) and L050 (CI for the same 0.382).

clusters.title: Spectral HVG panel was enriched for the same databases used to score it
clusters.description: The HVG panel gives priority to TRRUST TFs, STRING genes and canonical markers (343 TFs + 787 targets), and then PPI, TF-vs-target and B-cell prec@10 are scored against those same sources. The Geneformer B-cell prec@10 = 0.273 'non-replication' (paper 0.000) is measured on this marker-rich set, so it is not comparable. The summary notes the selection but does not account for it in conclusions. The within-panel permutation nulls limit, but do not remove, the effect.

clusters.title: SV3 PPI significance reported as both 3/12 and 10/12 layers
clusters.description: Under the run's BH correction SV3 pairs_700 is significant at 3/12 layers (L7, L9, L11; L10 also passes for pairs_900, so 4 layers counting both pair sets); raw p<0.05 holds at 9/12. The updated table and spec audit say '10/12 sig', which is an uncorrected z>2 count from the hub-confound file. Both appear without saying they use different rules. SV3 was also picked post hoc as the best of 7 axes x 2 pair sets. The 'weaker PPI' verdict is unchanged.

clusters.title: 'MaxToki layer-0 SV1 PPI z=5.62' is really SV7, a max over axes and pair sets
clusters.description: The cross-model PPI convergence cites 'MaxToki SV1 z=5.62 at layer 0'. 5.62 is the maximum over 7 axes x 2 pair sets and sits on SV7 pairs_900; SV1 at L0 is z=3.34 (p_bh 0.050) and SV1's maximum over all layers is 3.34. Mislabel plus max-selection. The verifier notes SV7 L0 still passes BH (0.026), so the convergence conclusion survives.

clusters.title: TF-vs-target 'jumps to 0.62 at L11 after ~0.53 at L0' is wrong
clusters.description: The joint SV2-SV7 AUROC is 0.596 at L0 (perm p 0.0099, significant), 0.610 at L6 and 0.620 at L11. The '~0.53' matches only the SV2_SV4 column. The profile is flat with a dip, not a late peak, so 'peak at different depth' and 'the depth-regime hypothesis is scGPT-specific' lose their support. The L11 value is also taken after the final norm, which partly overlaps L051.

clusters.title: TF-vs-target AUROC judged against 0.5 though its in-sample null is 0.54; no expression baseline
clusters.description: The centroid classifier is fit and scored on the same genes; its permutation null mean is 0.539-0.546 at every layer, but the summary anchors 'mean 0.572, non-trivially represented' to 0.5 and to the paper's 0.744. The CSV mean is 0.567, not 0.572. No expression or token-frequency baseline: 1-dropout alone gives AUROC 0.565 and mean expression 0.549 on the same 343 TFs vs 595 targets, and SV1 correlates with mean expression (|r| 0.43-0.50 at L2-L8) with no residualisation. The audits' multiplicity point does not hold (5/12 layers survive BH).

clusters.title: Spectral scorecard tallies do not match their own rows
clusters.description: The 29-row table says '11 ticks / 5 warnings / 13 crosses'; counting rows gives 10/5/14. The 22-row spec audit says '6/7/6/3'; counting gives 5/8/7/2.

clusters.title: Cell-type marker clustering 'replicated' only at static L0; L2-norm control misreported
clusters.description: 'Cell-type marker clustering is strong ... replicated (0.779 vs paper 0.851)' uses L0, the context-free token embedding; L1-L11 are 0.542-0.657. The L2-norm control quotes '0.580 (down from 0.779)', but 0.580 is the 12-layer mean after regression set against the L0 raw value; at L0 the residual is 0.648. '~25% of signal is magnitude-driven' uses raw AUROC as denominator; on above-chance signal it is 47% at L0 (71% by the summary's own comparison). L4 (0.473) and L11 (0.522) fall to chance. Same root idea as L047 (L0 is static), different analysis.

clusters.title: Stale scope lines in the spectral summary
clusters.description: The summary says 'Phases skipped: 8, 9a, 9b, 9c' while later sections report those phases as done. Persistent homology (9a) is described as skipped in one place and as run in another, and what was run is only kNN connected components.

clusters.title: Spectral number slips: GC-plasma angle and z-score read as odds ratio
clusters.description: The GC-plasma angle is reported as 72 to ~52 degrees; the L11 value is 46.4. The extracellular-space value 5.21 is a z-score in sv1_go_cc_copole.csv, but the audit row calls it 'OR=5.21' and compares it with the paper's OR=6.37.

clusters.title: 'Opposite of paper' hub-confound claim rests on 149 low-degree pairs with 0-2 hits
clusters.description: The low-degree group in phase4_hub_confound.csv has n=149 pairs with 0-2 co-pole pairs per layer (observed rate 0-0.0134). That cannot support the claim that the hub confound runs opposite to the paper.

clusters.title: Spectral autoloop iterations ran and gave results, but the summary says Phase 10 was not run
clusters.description: The summary says Phase 10 (autonomous loop) was 'NOT run ... deferred pending authorization'. The master log shows a run on 2026-05-05 with iterations 0002 and 0003 completed (H01-H03; H3-BC 'PROMISING' built on an 'early' stratum of N=14, H3-DEL, H3-G). These results are not reported. Iterations 0004-0005 failed (the audit overstated them). Partly overlaps L052, which covers the same autoloop's validation and stop-rule problems, not the omission.

clusters.title: 'Tissue-invariant gene geometry' counts the static L0 layer and uses only a gene-shuffle null
clusters.description: The 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel)' cross-tissue invariance averages 12 layer states including L0, the static token embedding, which is identical across tissues by construction (Pearson 1.000, top-1 1.0, best_layer = 0 for all pairs). The only null is a gene-label shuffle; there is no static-embedding floor, within-tissue split-half ceiling or random-init control. Similarity falls with depth (lung vs external-lung top-1 1.0 to 0.25 at L11; immune vs external-lung Pearson 0.448 at L10), which contradicts 'the trained transformer doesn't introduce tissue-specific divergence'. Shared genes are 75/168/77. Dropping L0 lowers the means only by about 0.01-0.03 (to about 0.85/0.75/0.72), so the error is the invariance claim and the 'strong/novel' label, not the means. Same mechanism as L047 (spectral CKA at L0), different pipeline and claim.

clusters.title: Immune domain built differently (98% TFs, 2,000 cells) and not disclosed
clusters.description: The immune domain reuses the spectral-geometry gene pool, which ranks TFs first with no TF cap: 343/350 genes are TRRUST TFs and 6 are markers. Lung has 87/382 TFs and 43 markers; external-lung 86/380 and 39. Immune also comes from 2,000 cells, while the summaries/ copy says 1,500. The summaries do not discuss this. Cross-domain contrasts are confounded by pool make-up: immune H123 1/12 vs lung 0/12, H139 'only immune passes', H-hub among 343 TFs, H-lineage marker counts, and immune negatives that are 99.95% TF-containing vs about 40% elsewhere. Within-domain results are not invalidated.

clusters.title: H-hub (z about 2.3 in 2 of 3 domains) called 'the strongest new result'
clusters.description: TF degree vs kNN centrality gives Spearman 0.060 (z 1.31, lung, n.s.), 0.118 (z 2.34, immune) and 0.115 (z 2.36, external-lung), from 100 permutations at one layer (L6) and one k (12). The null permutes degree uniformly with no control for expression, token frequency or literature bias; in lung/external-lung non-TFs get degree 0, so it partly measures TF vs non-TF, and immune is 343/350 TFs (N46). It is still called 'the strongest new result' and 'MaxToki does place regulatory hubs at central positions'. The tables do say 'weak-positive', and BH over 3 domains may still pass, so the error is the framing and the missing confound control.

clusters.title: H-lineage 'ext-lung 4/4 lineages significant' includes a B-cell result at the null p95
clusters.description: External-lung B-cell has 3 markers and observed purity 0.0556, equal to the null p95 (0.0556): 2 hits in 36 neighbour slots. Its 'significance' comes from a Gaussian z (3.05) on a discrete, zero-heavy null; the empirical p is at least about 0.05. So '4/4 lineages sig (all z>3)' should be 3/4. The nulls are random gene sets of the same size, with no control for co-expression or expression level, though lineage markers are co-expressed. Other lineages pass by wide margins.

clusters.title: H23 Forman 'replicates and validates the implementation' with no CI (all CIs include 0.5)
clusters.description: The pass rule is just AUROC < 0.45 on 52-123 kNN edges with 11-22 positives. Reproduced bootstrap CIs: lung 0.352 [0.18, 0.53], immune 0.416 [0.29, 0.54], external-lung 0.340 [0.16, 0.54]; all include 0.5. 'DIRECTIONAL REPLICATES ... Validates the spec implementation' is overstated. The summary also says the AUROCs are 'exactly in range 0.34-0.39' though immune is 0.42.

clusters.title: H-depth labelled 'NON-TRIVIAL' though not significant; exploratory batch uncorrected
clusters.description: H-depth is labelled 'NON-TRIVIAL' while the text admits it does not beat its feature-shuffle null. It sits in a batch of more than 10 exploratory tests (6 in the table plus Phase 4, H139, the H124 chain, H-cross and 4 autoloop tests) with no FDR correction.

clusters.title: Topology pair table: TF-only positives vs random negatives, STRING-only pairs labelled negative
clusters.description: Positives are TRRUST pairs, so 100% contain a TF; random negatives contain a TF 39-41% of the time (lung, external-lung). STRING-only pairs (48/24/61) are labelled 0. The spec asks for co-expression-matched and TF/target-degree-matched negatives; none exist. Any feature tracking TF identity, degree or PPI closeness moves the AUROC, which makes below-chance readings (triangle defect -0.055, H16 0.477-0.498) hard to read. The verifier notes delta-AUROC vs co-expression on the same pairs partly cancels this, and the immune domain gives the same verdicts, so headline negatives are unlikely to flip.

clusters.title: Run-folder topology FINAL_SUMMARY is stale (says run phases were SKIPPED)
clusters.description: The run-folder FINAL_SUMMARY still lists Phase 4 cross-model CCA, the Phase 11 autoloop and the H124-H138 annotation chain as SKIPPED, and says Layer 1 'cannot be evaluated'. The README and EXTENDED_FINDINGS report all of these as run (Phase 14 CCA r=0.78, scGPT r=0.40) and Layer 1 as 'partially replicates'. The summaries/ copy says 'PARTIALLY REPLICATES' in its text but 'SKIPPED' in its own table and 'not run' at line 89. Documentation only.

clusters.title: Topology TL;DR numbers wrong: 'Eucl ~ Geo (~0)' and 'H91 delta ~ +0.01'
clusters.location: runs/topology-141-217M/FINAL_SUMMARY.md:15 (TL;DR) vs its own Layer-3 row and hierarchy_summary.csv; Phase 9 JSON (H91 mean AUCs)
clusters.description: The TL;DR says Euclidean and geodesic distances are both about 0 over co-expression; the computed domain means average -0.035 for each, as the same file's L3 row shows. It says H91 is 'delta ~ +0.01 over chance'; external-lung mean AUC is 0.545 (domains 0.500/0.514/0.545). The summaries/ copy keeps 'delta ~ +0.01'.

clusters.title: Other wrong statements in the run-folder topology summary (diffusion strict audit, iter_05, iter_03)
clusters.description: (1) Diffusion distance on lung is said to fail the strict max-null audit, but it passes at L6 (strict margin +0.026, passes_strict=1). (2) iter_05 is said to 'rule out the popularity confound' for an H123 signal that is at or below chance in every stratum (AUC 0.29-0.53, mean delta -0.11). (3) iter_03 is said to confirm that a 'small phase-6 triangle-defect positive' is co-expression driven, but lung triangle-defect was -0.036 (verifier: debatable, L8 is +0.015). (4) The Phase-0 block omits the immune domain. Different iterations from L057/L058 (iter_04).

clusters.title: Diffusion time chosen on the evaluation pairs in every domain, including external-lung
clusters.description: For each domain the code loops over DIFF_TIMES and picks t by the best raw TRRUST AUROC on the same pairs it then reports, including external-lung, which the spec forbids. Since the co-expression AUROC does not depend on t, this directly maximises the reported delta. With 4 t values the inflation is modest, but the 'single relative positive' (diffusion on lung +0.023) is selected in-sample.

clusters.title: Triangle-defect spectrum collapsed to one signed sum, contrary to spec
clusters.description: The spec asks for a per-edge multi-scale triangle-defect feature vector. The code sums it over k into one scalar with an assumed direction. Raw AUROC is 0.46-0.52 and diffusion beats triangle-defect, which the spec's own diagnostic (line 547) says means the triangle-defect implementation is broken. So the 'paper-strongest feature is anti-predictive (-0.055)' non-replication may be an implementation artefact.

clusters.title: Manifold headline not shown to need MaxToki: extracted head does not beat simple PCA/avg-pool
clusters.description: The headline 'MaxToki-217M internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold ... first affirmative deployable result' (and 'multi-axis biological hub') is not qualified by the run's own Phase 12 LITE benchmark. Mean branch balanced accuracy: pca10 0.844, svd10 0.837, frozen avg-pool 0.792, extracted_z10 0.756; pseudotime 0.509 vs 0.262. No BH-significant difference against PCA/SVD/avg-pool (z10-pca10 -0.088, q 0.26); the only win is over 'raw_log1p' (0.142), a degenerate baseline. §11 admits no advantage; the headline and §10 omit it. Important correction to most audits: in phase12_anchor_benchmark_lite.py:92-95, pca10, svd10 and raw_log1p are all built from MaxToki avg-pooled hidden-state centroids (290x12x1232), not from raw expression (checked in code). So no expression-only or random-init baseline was ever run, and the quality gates were never applied to any baseline; model-specificity is untested rather than disproven. The H95/H103/H38 sweep manifolds were never compared with any baseline. Partly overlaps L067 (shuffled null passes two of four gates).

clusters.title: Manifold rulers are lookups of cell-type labels on cell-type centroid anchors
clusters.description: Anchors are donor x tissue x cell-type centroids. The H65 stage DAG and the H38-LITE, H92, H95 and H103 rulers are deterministic functions of cell-type labels. The nulls shuffle those labels globally. So any representation that separates cell types passes, and the 'multi-axis biological hub' and sweep positives say nothing specific about developmental structure. The spec requires 'ground truth independent of co-expression' (pipelines/manifold-discovery-extraction-compactification.md:600). Partly overlaps L068 (trustworthiness is not a biological check); the label-derived ruler problem is separate.

clusters.title: Phase 17 'partially orthogonal / rotates away' is explained by imperfect fits
clusters.description: The H95 head 'actively rotates away from H65 by 0.173' is read from cross-head correlation 0.642 being below ruler overlap 0.814. With self-fits 0.986 (H65) and 0.825 (H95), attenuation alone predicts about 0.814 x 0.986 x 0.825 = 0.662, close to 0.642. There is one training run per head, no seed or bootstrap spread. The 'null check' cannot show H95 is 'genuinely encoded': the scrambled-ruler head's self-fit equals the real one to 7 decimals (0.8247876), so in-sample self-fit does not discriminate, and the null's low cross-head 0.022 follows from scrambling. The PARTIALLY_ORTHOGONAL verdict and 'first quantitative support for the multi-axis hub' are not established.

clusters.title: Per-head 'operators' are o_proj slices; head attribution is not what heads compute
clusters.description: The single-head feature is the post-layer residual centroid projected onto head h's W_O columns. No Q/K/V or attention pattern is involved, and for L10 the input is centroid index 11, the post-final-norm state. Every input still needs a full forward pass, contrary to the spec's 'no forward pass' operator. 'Top-1 L10H6, H65 information concentrated in late-layer heads' and the contrast with scGPT's L2H5 describe late-layer residuals, not head computation. No random-projection control was run. §2 also mislabels these as 'value-projection operators'. The spec and paper use weight-derived operators too, so the method comparison is like-for-like; the head-level wording is wrong. Partly overlaps L079 (operator sizes and the 2,400x figure mislabelled in the paper).

clusters.title: Lung negative control gets random stage labels, so any feature set fails it
clusters.description: The non-hematopoietic lung control assigns each anchor a uniformly random stage label (checked in code). Any predictor would fail a ruler made of random labels, so the control cannot answer 'are the gates too loose?' or show the result is not generic tissue covariance, yet the summary (§5, §10) uses it that way. Partly overlaps L070 (control reported as failing 3 of 4 gates), L071 (first control passed and was rebuilt) and L122 (trust depends on anchor count); the random-label design is not in those rows.

clusters.title: Longevity: 'MaxToki beats HVG-PCA, encodes something beyond expression' from two below-chance scores
clusters.description: Balanced accuracy is 0.2755 for MaxToki L5 and 0.1722 for HVG-PCA-50; chance for 3 classes is 0.333 and the permutation null mean is 0.332. Comparing two below-chance numbers cannot show MaxToki 'is encoding something beyond raw expression PCA'. Age is a donor label: 17 donors split 10/4/3, so donor-level CV has almost no power. The main conclusion (gate fails, stop) is unaffected and the small cohort is disclosed. Same section as L083 (no positive control), different error.

verifications.error_type: wrong statistic (multiple-testing family chosen after looking at the results)
verifications.audit_pattern: P5 (closest fit: tests are filtered on their own outcome, overlap>=2 and p<0.1, before the BH step; no checklist item covers multiple-testing families directly)
verifications.deterministic_evidence:
CODE. runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phases2_to_8.py:183-187 skips tests with overlap x<2 and keeps a row only if p<0.1. Line 195 then runs fdr_bh on those kept rows only. Line 196 keeps q<0.05. full_12layer_pipeline.py:243-252 does the same thing. This script wrote the current phase2/layer_*/significant_enrichments.csv files. The BH step is one pooled run over the kept rows of all features. The spec, pipelines/sparse-autoencoders/01-sae-atlas.md:182, asks for BH "across all terms tested for that feature".

RECOMPUTE (CPU only, about 30 s). I rebuilt the 2,377 filtered terms (the same count as full_12layer.log:6) from the same GO/KEGG/Reactome/TRRUST files and the Replogle var symbols. I took the top-20 lists from phase2/layer_XX/feature_catalog.json. Then I computed every feature x term hypergeometric p with the same N, K and n. Applying the code's own rule (x>=2, p<0.1, pooled BH) reproduces the reported numbers exactly on all 12 layers: 2016/3685/3503/3364/3255/3340/3371/3430/3523/3442/3159/3040 annotated features, and the enrichment counts match too (L0 23,074; L5 27,661; L11 20,759). The kept tests are 26,997 (L0), 34,207 (L5) and 26,361 (L11), out of 5,937,746, 11,713,856 and 11,704,348 tests in total.

Results with a correct BH:
(a) Per-feature BH over all 2,377 terms, as the spec asks: L0 104/2498 = 4.2%, L1-L9 1.6-1.9%, L10 1.1%, L11 55/4924 = 1.1%. Reported rates were 80.7%, 74.8-67.8% and 61.7%.
(b) Global BH over all feature x term tests: 29 features at L0, 5 at L5 and 0 at L11. Layers L6-L8, L10 and L11 have 0.
(c) The largest raw p among the saved "significant" rows is 0.039-0.042 on every layer. So the step is close to no correction at all.
(d) 79-85% of the significant rows rest on an overlap of only 2 genes in a top-20 list. Under per-feature BH, a 2-gene overlap can never pass: its smallest p is about 1e-4, and the rank-1 threshold is 0.05/2377 = 2.1e-5.
(e) Phase 6 needs 50 "richly annotated" features with 3 or more enrichments. Under per-feature BH, only 43 features at L5 qualify, against 2,384 under the code's rule.

WHAT CAUSES THE INFLATION. Removing only the p<0.1 filter, while still dropping tests with overlap<2, gives 80.3%/66.0%/59.8%. So the p<0.1 filter in the title adds only 0.4-2 points. Almost all of the inflation comes from leaving the overlap 0 and 1 tests out of the BH step. The reference repo does the same: repos/bio-sae/src/04_annotate_features.py:140-141 drops tests with overlap<2, and BH runs at :316. That means the Geneformer 52.4% comparator is not FDR-controlled either, and its background set is different. Either way, the MaxToki annotation rates are not FDR-controlled and fall to 1-4% under the spec's own procedure.

LEDGER. There is no matching row. The sae-atlas rows L020-L032 and L123 cover TF-specificity, Phase 6/8t layers and GATA1, not Phase 2 annotation.

Those claims live in summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:19-27, :79, :92 ("excellent biological annotation (68-81%)"), :226 and in FINAL_SUMMARY_12layer.md:9-27. They cannot stand. Apply BH per feature over all 2,377 terms, as 01-sae-atlas.md:182 says. Report global BH as a sensitivity check. Apply any overlap>=2 or p filter only after the correction, as a reporting filter. This needs about 30 s of CPU and no model forward pass.

4. Re-derive every downstream selection from the corrected labels: Phase 6 rich features, Phase 10 annotated/unannotated split, Stage-2 sources and coherence, Stage-3 Exp-1 split and Exp-2 triplets. Those downstream re-runs need forward passes. Most of them are already queued for other bugs (L011, L031, L123), so they should use the corrected labels.

verifications.error_type: contradictory claims; missing null; metric driven by shared random initialisation (by-construction artifact)
verifications.audit_pattern: P1
verifications.deterministic_evidence:
1) The contradiction is real. The 3-layer summary (summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:41-46, 82-83, and again at :229) says "Features are overwhelmingly layer-specific - no persistent scaffold. Replicates" and gives it a tick, based on L0->L5 125/4928 (2.5%) and L5->L11 26/4928 (0.5%). That number is compared with the paper's ADJACENT L0->L1 2.5%. The 12-layer summary of the same SAEs (sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY_12layer.md:28-37, 49) says "dramatically higher cross-layer persistence than Geneformer ... differs from paper". It reports L6->L7 21.5% and L0->L8 13.3%. The tick was never changed. The pipeline spec's own check (pipelines/sparse-autoencoders/01-sae-atlas.md:628) says a match rate above 5% at any layer means something is wrong. The 12-layer run hits 21.5% and nobody acted on it. The spec also asks for a shuffle null and a test on adjacent layers only (:268-270). The 3-layer run did neither.
2) The numbers are wrong in places. I recomputed persistence from the saved checkpoints (outputs/phase1/layer_XX/sae_final.pt). My counts match the log exactly: L0->L1 0/4928, L1->L2 8, L2->L3 45, L6->L7 1059, L0->L5 125, L0->L8 654, L5->L11 26. The 12-layer summary instead says L0->L1 0.5%, L1->L2 3.3% and L2->L3 1.6%. The correct values are 0.0%, 0.2% and 0.9%. The denominator counts all 4928 decoder columns, including dead ones (phases2_to_8.py:292). At L0, 2430 of those features are dead.
3) New finding: both verdicts are mostly caused by the training setup, not by the model. Every layer's SAE is trained with the same seed, 42 (setup/topk_sae.py:71 and :79; full_12layer_pipeline.py:170-176 passes no seed). The decoder starts as a copy of the encoder (topk_sae.py:31-34). So all 12 SAEs start from the same random decoder matrix. Training runs only 900 steps, so trained features keep a median cosine of about 0.3 to their starting vector. Dead features keep it at 1.0: 2433 L0 columns are still above 0.99.

I used the same annotation rule as experiment1_exhaustive.py:83-94: a feature counts as annotated if it has at least one row in sae-atlas phase2/layer_05/significant_enrichments.csv.

(1) Unannotated features are at parity. They are not over-represented.
- The traced pool is 500 annotated + 500 unannotated by design, so the base rate is 50%.
- Top-20 hubs: 11/20 annotated (55%). Fisher test against the other 980 features: OR 1.23, p = 0.82.
- Top-100: 45/100 annotated, p = 0.34.
- Top-50: 27/50 annotated, p = 0.66.
- Top-10: 9/10 annotated, p = 0.02. So the very top leans toward annotated features, not away from them.
- Unannotated features hold 49.98% of all 4,970,096 edges. Their design share is 50%.
- Median edges per feature: 4,967 for annotated, 4,968 for unannotated. Mann-Whitney test p = 0.22.
- The whole edge range is 4,900 to 5,400 (CV 0.5%). These counts come from the block-deletion artefact already logged as L011.
- "Fisher's exact test: not significant" was never computed anywhere. It is typed as text in stage3_synthesize.py:131. My recomputed test agrees that it is not significant.

(2) The Phase 6 features are as central as every other feature. 47 of the 50 Phase 6 features (sae-atlas outputs/phase6/causal_patching.csv) were among the 1,000 traced in Exp 1. Their median edge rank is 497 of 1,000, and one of them is rank 2. Mean edges: 4,973 for these 47 vs 4,970 for the rest, Mann-Whitney p = 0.98. So the claim that "the annotated subset is not representative of the computationally central population" (sae-atlas summary, current line 280) is contradicted by the same data.

(3) Pool rate. The text says "~50% unannotated pool". The L5 atlas catalogue actually has 3,340/4,928 features annotated (67.8%), or 3,080/4,555 among active features (67.6%). That makes about 32% unannotated. The 50% is only the Exp-1 design split.

(4) Phase 6 count. The text says Phase 6 tested "30 richly-annotated features". It used 50: phase6/summary.json n_features = 50; phase6_patching.py:40 N_FEATURES = 50; the summary's own Phase 6 section, current line 241. The 30 is Stage 2's per-layer count (circuit_summary.json n_features_per_layer = 30).

(5) Side check. The exhaustive summary says "~5K edges/feature in both experiments". Stage 2 actually has 2,144,011 / 120 = 17,867 edges per feature.

CODE. setup/maxtoki_adapter.py:142-151 orders genes by falling normalised expression. The model is LlamaForCausalLM (causal), so a query can only attend to keys earlier in the sequence. runs/attention-grn-217M/scripts/phase0_extract.py:292-304 adds attention for every ordered HVG pair and adds 1 to pair_counts for every cell that has both genes. Lines :326-328 divide by pair_counts, so cells where the mask forces a zero are counted in the average. phase1_trivial_baselines.py:231 and :276 use only attn[pert,:]. phase3_residualization.py:115-130 uses only edge_matrix[tf_i]. A grep of every script finds no transposed or symmetrised attention edge. phase0b builds a symmetric value-vector cosine, which is a different object; its best knockdown AUROC is 0.515.

REBUILT TOKEN ORDER (K562 217M, 2,000 control cells, tokeniser only, no forward pass; script in scratchpad n20/order_counts_k562.py). pair_counts were reproduced exactly. Let C[A,B] be the number of cells where B comes before A. C + C^T equals pair_counts on every off-diagonal pair, so in each cell exactly one direction is allowed. The saved edge therefore satisfies E[P,T] = F[P,T] x (mean attention over the allowed cells), where F is the share of cells in which T outranks P. Spearman(E, F) is 0.41 across all pairs, and the median within a row is 0.50.

KNOCKDOWN ENDPOINT, K562 (174 perturbations, mean per-perturbation AUROC):
- deployed forward edge: 0.512
- F alone, which uses no model: 0.517 (Wilcoxon p = 0.068 against forward)
- rank-conditioned edge: 0.496
- transpose: 0.484
- target variance: 0.596

So on this endpoint the deployed attention edge does no better than a model-free rank statistic.

4) The alignment itself holds. The excess over the gene-median null is 0.299 (about 300 SD). After double-centring the cosine matrices the Pearson is 0.380. verifications.deterministic_evidence:
FACTS THAT ARE TRUE
- runs/spectral-geometry-217M/scripts/phase0_extract.py:97-152 gives priority to TRRUST/STRING/58-marker genes. The top-variance fill (:144-150) only runs if the pool is smaller than 1500.
- outputs/phase0.log shows 'reference-annotated pool: 3766', 'priority HVG selected: 1500', 'priority_in_HVG=1500 trrust_tfs=343 trrust_targets=787 canonical_markers=40'. So 100% of the panel comes from the scoring databases. The fill step never ran.
- I rebuilt the panel from the h5ad (seed 42, 2000 cells). It matches outputs/phase0/gene_features.csv exactly.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ERROR
(1) The source design does the same. pipelines/residual-stream-spectral-geometry.md:61 says the paper's primary tests run on a '195-gene submatrix: intersection of the full vocabulary with annotated genes in TRRUST, STRING, and GO'. Its B-cell markers are also hand-picked (:63, :292).

(2) The selection never looks at the embeddings. It uses only database membership and expression variance. Every null shuffles labels or genes inside the same panel: phases_345.py:74-78, :101-107, :274-277; phase9b_cross_model.py:212-222, :268-277. Choosing genes this way cannot create pair-level structure in the embeddings.

(3) Direct test. I used the static (layer-0) embedding tables, read from the weights only (no forward pass), and scored two panels:
- (A) the run's panel;
- (B) a plain top-variance panel of in-vocabulary genes with the same 11 B-cell markers added. Only 529 of its 1500 genes overlap with A, and only 35% are annotated.

Panel A reproduces the published numbers exactly: Geneformer B-cell prec@10 0.2727 (null 0.0061, z 26.96); Geneformer static PPI SV3 z 5.03 (844 pairs); cross-model Pearson 0.382.

Panel B gives:
- Geneformer B-cell prec@10 0.2818 (z 27.82), slightly higher;
- MaxToki static prec@10 0.1545 on both panels (z 14.5 vs 14.3);
- static PPI best z 6.96 (81 pairs) for both models, also higher.

So the annotated panel does not inflate these scores.

(4) The panel is not 'marker-rich' compared with the paper. B-cell marker density is 11/1500 = 0.73% here vs 7/195 = 3.6% in the paper's set. The chance level is lower here (null 0.006), not higher.

(5) The summary does disclose the selection: summaries/spectral-geometry-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:170-174. It also qualifies the B-cell conclusion at :262 ('On our 1500-HVG, immune-marker-rich gene set ... The paper's negative may have been gene-set-specific').

A SEPARATE REAL ISSUE (not caused by the panel)
The 0.273 vs the paper's 0.000 compares different metrics:
- the run (phase9b_cross_model.py:251-266) averages per-gene top-10 neighbours over 11 genes, 5 of them TFs (BACH2, BCL6, PRDM1, IRF4, IRF8);
- the spec (:292) uses the 10 nearest neighbours of the B-cell centroid of 7 markers.

The spec's centroid version is useless on these embeddings: observed 0.6 = null 0.6, z 0, on both panels and both models. The scorecard row '❌ clustering IS present' (summary :257, :298, :343) is therefore not a fair comparison. That belongs with the cross-model findings (F23/F17/F26), not with the panel choice.

No ledger row covers the panel selection. Scratch scripts: <AGENT_TMP>/<SESSION_DIR>/d422dc33-6d6f-4b2b-bbf7-f274d8a82fae/scratchpad/n34_analyse2.py and n34_centroid.py.

- Shuffling the group labels across pairs: one-sided p = 0.21, two-sided p = 0.37. Pair bootstrap 95% CI of the difference in hits per pair is [-0.028, 0.089], which includes 0.

Power: suppose the low group had exactly the high group's per-layer rate. You would then expect only 4.2 of 12 layers with z > 2 (2 were seen). The low group would need 2 or more hits out of 149 to pass z > 2. At equal enrichment, the z ratio is sqrt(149/695) = 0.46, so the expected low z is about 1.44 against the high group's 3.10. Both groups sit above their null: low is 2.45x enriched, high is 3.64x. So the low group is not null. It is just too small to measure well.

Caveat: I also ran a continuous test, the Spearman correlation between the larger endpoint degree and hits per pair. It gives rho = 0.128, gene-permutation p = 0.002. So a properly powered test may still find some degree dependence. The reported split cannot show it, though, and cannot show an "opposite of paper" reversal.

Small extra point: seeds use hash(name) % 10000 (lines 148 and 173). Python randomises string hashes in each process, so the per-group null draws cannot be repeated exactly.

verifications.error_type: unsupported claim (a result labelled positive with no null of its own, plus no multiple-testing correction across the exploratory batch)
verifications.audit_pattern: P9 (claim stronger than the evidence). It also has P1 parts (H-depth has no null of its own) and P5 parts (no correction across the batch).
verifications.deterministic_evidence:
1) H-depth was never tested against a null. In runs/topology-141-217M/scripts/phase16_lineage_hub_depth.py:260-267, H-depth only computes total_h1 and twonn_dim for each layer. The summary block (:326-340) only stores the raw per-layer lists. There is no shuffle, permutation or comparison.

2) The only null that exists for H1 is Phase 5's feature-shuffle null (outputs/phase5/h01_h03_persistent_homology.csv). That null shuffles each column on its own (phase123_splits_nulls.py:161-167). Its mean per-layer trajectory has the same three-phase shape that EXTENDED_FINDINGS.md:20 calls "NON-TRIVIAL" and "reproducible". In every domain the null peaks at L5 within L0-L7, drops at L6-L7, then rises over L8-L11. Lung null means: 6, 65, 86, 110, 118, 129, 114, 92, 93, 112, 142, 210. I correlated the observed H1 trajectory with the null-mean trajectory. Spearman is 0.895 (lung), 0.762 (immune) and 0.846 (ext-lung); Pearson is 0.93, 0.83 and 0.78. Observed H1 beats the null's 95th percentile at only 1, 1 and 0 of 12 layers. So the shape comes from the per-coordinate spread of each layer, not from any gene-specific structure. Three domains from the same model showing the same shape is not evidence either.

3) The table text is also wrong in detail. It says "partial recovery L8-L11" and "peak ~150-210". In lung and immune, L11 (204, 231) is higher than the L5 'peak' (162, 210).

4) The intrinsic-dimension half of H-depth is a bug, and its results were dropped without comment. twonn_intrinsic_dim reorders the empirical CDF by the unsorted mu (`F = F[np.argsort(mu)]`), then fits it against sorted mu. On synthetic data of known dimension 2, 5 and 10 it returns +0.11, +0.20 and -0.22; a corrected version returns 2.10, 3.94 and 8.94. The saved values are negative at 4/12, 9/12 and 7/12 layers. No summary reports them.

5) No topology script applies any multiple-testing correction. grep for multipletests, fdr, benjamini, bonferroni and holm finds nothing in scripts/*.py. H-hub calls a result 'significant' when |z| > 1.96, uncorrected (:352), using 100 permutations.

6) I reran H-hub and it reproduces exactly (rho 0.0604, 0.1184, 0.1155). With 10,000 permutations, the two-sided p is 0.244 (lung), 0.026 (immune) and 0.026 (ext-lung). BH over the 3 hub tests gives q = 0.039. Over the 10 Phase-16 tests it gives q = 0.033. Over a wider batch of about 25 z-tests it gives q of about 0.031. Holm gives 0.078 (3 tests) and 0.104 (10 tests). So the 'no correction' charge is true. It changes the H-hub verdict under FWER (family-wise error rate) control, which Holm uses. It does not change it under BH. Either way, p = 0.026 does not support 'the strongest new result' (EXTENDED_FINDINGS.md:58). Also, the immune pool is 343 of 350 TFs (h_hub_tf_degree.csv).

No existing ledger row covers H-depth, TwoNN, H-hub or Phase-16 multiplicity. L057 is a different relabel: H-cross (iter_04) labelled 'NOVEL POSITIVE'.

verifications.error_type: Implementation does not match the spec or the source code. The triangle-defect feature was rebuilt with a fixed sign that is the opposite of the source's, and the 3 scales were summed into one number. As a result, the run summary wrongly calls the feature "anti-predictive (-0.055)", and the paper quotes a cross-layer number (0.275) that only holds for this non-faithful feature.
verifications.audit_pattern: P3 (the endpoint does not match the object of the claim: the run scores a different feature, with a different sign, against a different comparator than the paper's triangle-defect spectrum, then calls it a non-replication). P6 is secondary: the negative was declared without checking the port against the source code.
verifications.deterministic_evidence:
CODE. runs/topology-141-217M/scripts/phase6_manifold_distances.py:245-251 sums triangle_defect_feature(E,k) over k=8,12,16 and scores it with direction="larger_is_positive". In the feature function (:95-120), the distance is Euclidean and not normalised. Third points come from the overlap of the two kNN lists. When the lists do not overlap, it falls back to pool[:k] (line 115), which picks the LOWEST GENE INDICES, not the nearest genes.

SPEC. pipelines/topology-geometry-141-hypotheses.md:278 asks for "a per-edge feature vector" across scales. Line 547 says that if diffusion beats triangle-defect, the implementation is broken.

SOURCE. repos/topology-biomechinterp2/iterations/iter_0028/run_iter0028_screen.py:884-946 and :1692-1708 do it differently in 4 ways:
- Geodesic kNN distances (n_neighbors=12).
- Third points are the k nodes with the smallest d(u,w)+d(v,w).
- The defect is normalised, (d_uw+d_vw-d_uv)/d_uv, and clipped at 0.
- Five summaries are built from q50, q90 and the fraction of defects at or below 0.05, then scored with SMALLER defect as regulatory: zscore(-median_mean), zscore(-tail_mean), +zscore(close_frac).
So the port's sign is the opposite of the source's. The source's +0.026 is a gain over a baseline score, not a difference from co-expression. The pre-audit summary (summaries/topology-141-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:86) still claims the feature was "built per the source paper recipe (... sum across scales)".

RECOMPUTED (36 domain-layer rows, from saved PCA-20 embeddings, CPU only):
- I reproduced the stored triangle AUROC exactly (max difference 5.6e-17). Domain means as coded: lung 0.510, immune 0.457, external-lung 0.518. Overall 0.495, which is -0.0547 vs co-expression (0.550). Diffusion is 0.562.
- Each single scale alone gives 0.493 to 0.498, so summing the scales is not what drives the result.
- With the sign learned in 5-fold cross-validated logistic regression on the 3-scale vector: 0.5395, so -0.010 vs co-expression. By domain: immune +0.017, lung -0.033, external-lung -0.014. The cross-validated summed scalar gives 0.5416, about the same as the vector, so the sign is the driver.
- Source-faithful features (9-dim vector plus geodesic distance, cross-validated): 0.5419, so -0.008 vs co-expression.
- With the source's own fixed weights and no annotation term: 0.499 alone and 0.526 with the geodesic baseline.
- Diffusion still beats the triangle feature in 21 to 23 of 36 layers under the faithful or learned-sign versions (32 of 36 as coded). No version beats co-expression on average.
- H123 null-gap counts are the same with or without the triangle term: 0, 1 and 0 positive layers for external-lung, immune and lung, in both phase78 CSVs.
- main.tex 0.275: the summed port feature reproduces it exactly (lung 0.187, immune 0.409, external-lung 0.228). The source-faithful feature gives 0.459 (median defect) to 0.480 (source score) mean cross-layer Pearson.

Scratch script: <AGENT_TMP>/<SESSION_DIR>/d422dc33-6d6f-4b2b-bbf7-f274d8a82fae/scratchpad/n56_tri_check.py (results in n56_tri_check_lung_immune_external_lung_all.csv).

BOTTOM LINE. The claim is half right. The "-0.055, anti-predictive" label comes from the code: about -0.045 of the -0.055 goes away once the sign is learned. But the non-replication itself still holds. The paper's +0.026 and the claim that triangle-defect is the strongest metric do not reproduce under any version I tried.

With that many ties, the highest Spearman any untied score can reach is 0.8247876. The reported H95 self-fit (0.8247876079) is exactly that ceiling. The head can fit any 4-class split of 208 anchors in a 2,464-dim feature space, so in-sample self-fit cannot show H95 is "genuinely encoded".

(2) The gap is predicted by arithmetic. Breaking the H95 ties at random gives Spearman(D_h65, D_h95) = 0.6721 (sd 0.0022 over 20 draws). Multiplying by the H65 self-fit gives 0.663. The finding's estimate is 0.814 x 0.986 x 0.825 = 0.662. The observed 0.642 is close to both.

- HVG-PCA null: mean 0.356, SD 0.087, range 0.200-0.581. None of the 60 shuffles scored as low as 0.1722.

4. What the +0.103 gap means.
- MaxToki beats HVG-PCA in all 5 splits (0.267/0.211/0.302/0.299/0.298 vs 0.122/0.166/0.158/0.180/0.235).
- Under the donor-level null, the paired gap has mean -0.002 and SD 0.063. Only 1 of 60 shuffles reached +0.103.
- So the gap is not pure noise. But it comes from HVG-PCA being wrong more often than random guessing on the real age labels, more than in any shuffle. MaxToki is also below its own null.
- Being less wrong is not evidence that MaxToki encodes more. The sentence "encoding something beyond raw expression PCA" does not follow.
- The same reasoning is built into the code as a pass. run_stage1.py:196 sets `g1_pass_vs_baseline = best_ba > hvg_ba`. extraction_stats.json records it as true. report.md:38 prints "G1 (vs HVG-PCA baseline): PASS — beats by 10.3 pp".

5. The test has little power.
- sampled_obs.csv: 17 donors, one age per donor, ages 33-69 (the summary says 22-74). Donors split 10/4/3 across the bins.
- Every test split holds 5 donors from only 2 of the 3 bins.
- 3 of the 17 donors (TSP4, TSP6, TSP14) are never in a test set.
- The oldest bin has 3 donors. It appears in a test set in only 1 of the 5 splits, through 2 donors (TSP2, TSP7). TSP6 is never tested.
- The splits are 5 random 25% hold-outs, not "5-fold" CV as the summary says.

6. A small naming error. "HVG-PCA-50" (upstream lines 350-365) does not select HVGs (highly variable genes). It is an SVD without centring, run on all 60,606 genes of the already log-normalised matrix (max value 8.80, not whole numbers).

7. Ledger check. No ledger row covers this. L083 is the missing positive control (P6). L084 is the wrong claim that L5 is the shared layer. This is a different error in the same file.

verifications.recommended_fix:
Wording and logic fixes only. Nothing needs a model run.

1. FINAL_SUMMARY.md:44-47: delete "MaxToki L5 does beat ... beyond raw expression PCA". Replace it with: "Both MaxToki L5 (0.276) and the expression baseline (0.172) score below chance (1/3) and below a donor-level null (mean about 0.35). The gap between them shows the baseline is wrong more often, not that MaxToki encodes age or anything extra."

2. FINAL_SUMMARY.md:68-77: rewrite the explanation. The run's null sits at chance because it shuffles labels across cells, which breaks the donor structure. Add the donor-level null (MaxToki 0.353 ± 0.049; baseline 0.356 ± 0.087).

3. State the power problem:
- 17 donors split 10/4/3
- 3 donors are never tested
- the oldest bin is tested in only 1 of 5 splits
- the splits are 5 random 25% hold-outs, not 5-fold CV
- the sampled age range is 33-69, not 22-74.

5. In run_stage1.py:196, only count the baseline comparison when the probe is above chance or its null. Add a donor-level permutation null next to the cell-level one.

6. Rename "HVG-PCA-50" to "SVD-50 without centring, on all genes".

7. Optional: in main.tex:1008-1010, say the null is a cell-level shuffle, or cite the donor-level null.

The donor-level null runs from the cached maxtoki_layer_reps.npy in about 8 minutes on CPU (60 shuffles).
